first.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the emotionally obvious move, and memory_73 reports strong acquisition and revenue lift — but that same memory carries an explicit caveat: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition. That is exactly the kind of confound that inflates apparent lift, so I am spending one verification pull on memory_73 rather than acting on it. Discounting also carries the largest downstream risk to the primary objective: price cuts buy acquisition volume at the cost of per-account revenue quality, margin anchoring, and a segment that churns when the promo lapses, which is the opposite of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. I would only pursue it if the archive shows a clean, cohort-separated result.

My intended action is simplify_onboarding. Two independent memories point at it (memory_86 on shortened onboarding lifting completion and time-to-value, memory_31 on signup field reduction producing a durable SMB activation lift), and it maps directly onto the two internal metrics that are actually degrading: onboarding completion down 4% and activation down 6%. Onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a fix there plausibly addresses both declines with one experiment slot, whereas activation_messaging (memory_91) treats the downstream symptom only. Referral incentives (memory_57) depend on a healthy installed base and do nothing for the funnel leak; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is sound but addresses a segment that is not where the current bleeding is.

Second verification goes to memory_86 because it is the load-bearing evidence for my chosen action, it is 24 days old, and I should confirm it was measured on a comparable self-serve population before I lean on it. Caveat I am carrying forward: none of these memories were formed under active competitive price pressure, so the current declines may be partly demand-side rather than friction-side. Standard experiment scale with a proper holdout, and I want the readout to separate onboarding completion from activation so I can tell which mechanism moved rather than pooling them the way memory_73 apparently did.
